About me

Quiet discipline.
Genuine warmth.

My working life began in construction. I trained in Building Technology at the Federal Polytechnic, Ado-Ekiti — a National Diploma in 2003, then a Higher National Diploma in 2008 — and worked as an architectural draughtsman and later a site supervisor.

In 2010 I took a post as a Class Teacher at St. Michaels Group of Schools in Ijebu Owo, and I have stayed in education since.

A year later I was appointed Head Mistress of Faith Nursery and Primary School in Iyere Owo, where I led the school until 2016 — five years running a nursery and primary school, answerable for the staff, the pupils and their parents.

In 2024 my Postgraduate Diploma in Education was awarded through the National Teachers' Institute, Kaduna, affiliated to the University of Ilorin. The PGDE is the professional qualification that qualifies me to teach at secondary level, and my Building Technology background gives me two subjects I can teach with genuine depth: Basic Technology and Technical Drawing. My NABTEB certificate in Computer Craft Studies, together with daily work as a computer operator, adds Computer Studies.

I now live in Abuja and am looking for a full-time secondary teaching post — or a primary post where my leadership experience is useful.

“
A child who feels safe will try. A child who is allowed to try will learn. My work is to make room for both.
My approach in the classroom
What I believe

Three things I hold to.

No. 01

Structure first

Children settle once they know what the day holds. A clear routine comes before everything else; the confidence follows it.

No. 02

Patience with the slow reader

A child who is hurried learns to guess. Real time, real repetition, and no moving on until the ground is firm underneath them.

No. 03

Parents kept close

Five years as Head Mistress taught me that a child's week goes better when home and school agree. I keep families informed and involved.

What I teach

Two subjects, taught with authority.

A Building Technology background for the technical subjects, a computer qualification for ICT, and six years in schools — five of them leading one.
